title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Another tanker was hit on Wednesday evening, 6 nautical miles north of Khasab, and 44 ships are now holding in the Gulf. In the air, rates are at their highest of 2026 as peak season builds, and more airlines have pushed Saudi returns into December and January.

stories.headline: New tanker strike 6 nautical miles off Khasab; 44 ships now waiting
body: An unknown projectile hit a tanker's engine room about 6 nautical miles north of Khasab at 8:45pm Gulf time on Wednesday, UKMTO said. The crew were safe as of early Thursday. The ship and the attacker have not been named.

Straits Daily Brief counts 44 ships holding position in the Strait and Gulf, up from 43. Only 2 transits were logged on 15 November, against 85 a day before the crisis. Iran's navy claims three tankers hit mines east of the strait; no maritime authority has confirmed it.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: a third strike in three days, this one right off Musandam. Gulf sea schedules will not improve this month.

stories.headline: Two of this week's hit tankers are UAE-linked
body: Riviera reports that the tanker On Phoenix, hit off Oman on 16 November, is UAE-owned and AET-managed. The crude tanker Al Dhanna, owned and managed by ADNOC Logistics & Services, was hit in its steering gear room in the Gulf. Both crews were safe.
A separate NAVAREA report on 17 November logged another incident for On Phoenix near Ras Hindi. It is unclear if this was a second attack.
stories.soWhat: UAE-owned ships are now regular targets. UAE shippers will keep looking for land, air and east-coast routes.

stories.headline: Air freight rates hit their 2026 high as peak season starts
body: The TAC Index global measure (BAI00) rose 6.6% in the week to 9 November and is 28.2% above last year. Air Cargo Week says rates are now at their highest level of 2026.
Frankfurt outbound rose 9.9% in the week and is up 48.1% on last year. Europe saw what the report calls chunky gains on routes including the UAE.
stories.soWhat: Buy rates are rising into the busiest weeks of the year. Fixed-price air contracts lose margin fast in this market.

stories.headline: Saudi flight cuts stretch into December and January
body: flydubai has extended Riyadh and Abha cancellations to 27 November and resumed Dammam on a reduced schedule. Etihad's passenger and cargo cuts to Riyadh and Dammam run to 30 November.

Further out, Air France stays off Riyadh to 12 December, British Airways has pushed its London–Riyadh restart to 11 January, and Cathay Pacific Riyadh is suspended to 31 January. Qatar Airways resumed Riyadh and Dammam on 13 and 14 November.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: flydubai's dates and long-haul cuts into 2027. Belly space into Riyadh stays thin through the new year.

stories.headline: Talabat raises 2026 outlook again; GCC grows 9%
body: Talabat's Q3 GMV rose 17% to $3 billion, and revenue rose 18% to $1.2 billion. GCC markets, including the UAE, grew 9%, while Egypt, Jordan and Iraq grew 43%.
Adjusted EBITDA fell 3% to $150 million and net income fell 15% to $102 million. It is the second guidance upgrade this year.
stories.soWhat: Order volume keeps growing but margins are squeezed. Expect platforms to push hard on delivery partner rates.

competitors.name: Talabat
competitors.headline: Growth shifts outside the Gulf: non-GCC now 25% of GMV
body: Non-GCC markets made up 25% of Talabat's GMV in Q3, up from 20% a year earlier. Free cash flow rose 41% to $141 million.
Talabat runs its own rider network, so it is both a last-mile rival in quick commerce and a potential buyer of cross-border and warehousing services.
competitors.soWhat: Its fastest growth is in Egypt, Jordan and Iraq, where we have strong networks. That is the angle for a partnership pitch.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Q3 net profit Dh48m on record Dh1.98bn revenue
body: Still our latest figures: Q3 net profit rose to Dh48 million from Dh5.2 million, and revenue rose 24% to a record Dh1.98 billion. Freight forwarding led growth; gross margin was 21% against 23.2%.
competitors.soWhat: With air buy rates at their 2026 high, protecting forwarding margin matters more than chasing volume this quarter.

opportunities.title: Peak-season air yield
opportunities.text: Rates are at their 2026 high and still rising week on week. Reprice spot air quotes daily, not weekly.

opportunities.title: Saudi by road into 2027
opportunities.text: Air France, BA and Cathay are off Riyadh into December and January. Sell UAE–Saudi road as the steady option for the whole winter.

opportunities.title: Non-sea routes for UAE shippers
opportunities.text: UAE-owned tankers are being hit. Shippers with Gulf sea exposure need land and air alternatives now.

opportunities.title: Platforms growing outside the Gulf
opportunities.text: Talabat grew 43% in Egypt, Jordan and Iraq. Offer cross-border and fulfilment where our network is deep.

watchouts.title: Strikes closer to the UAE
watchouts.text: Wednesday's hit was 6 nautical miles off Khasab. Feeder and east-coast schedules may slip again.

watchouts.title: Unconfirmed mine claims
watchouts.text: Iran says three tankers hit mines. Even unverified, this keeps insurers and owners cautious.

watchouts.title: Air buy rates in peak
watchouts.text: Fixed-rate air contracts signed earlier in the year may now be below cost on some lanes.

watchouts.title: Platform rate pressure
watchouts.text: Talabat's profit fell while orders grew. Delivery partners should expect tougher rate talks.

watchouts.title: Long Saudi air gap
watchouts.text: Some carriers are out of Riyadh until late January. Customers relying on belly space need a plan beyond November.

moves.title: Daily air spot repricing through peak
moves.text: Move spot air quotes to a daily rate card while the TAC index climbs. Flag any fixed contract below current buy rate.

moves.title: Refresh the Saudi lane advisory
moves.text: Add flydubai to 27 Nov, Etihad to 30 Nov, Air France to 12 Dec, BA to 11 Jan and Cathay to 31 Jan. Offer road capacity in the same note.

moves.title: Call Gulf sea-exposed accounts
moves.text: After the Khasab strike, call top accounts on Gulf sea lanes with land and air options and a priced alternative.

moves.title: Talabat cross-border pitch
moves.text: Build a proposal for cross-border and fulfilment in Egypt, Jordan and Iraq, where Talabat is growing fastest.

moves.title: Floor for last-mile platform rates
moves.text: Set a minimum rate per drop before platform renewals, as margin-squeezed platforms push on price.
